scores.thesis: World-class franchise with enormous installed base, services annuity, and best-in-class capital returns, but at $4.6T market cap a 100x outcome is mathematically impossible. Compounder-quality, not satellite-quality.
catalysts: Services margin expansion
On-device AI upgrade cycle
Continued mega-scale buybacks
risks: Regulatory pressure on App Store economics
China demand and supply concentration
Hardware innovation stagnation
scores.pass_reason: Mega-cap size precludes 100x; not a micro/small-cap satellite candidate.

scores.thesis: Dominant enterprise software and cloud moat with high ROIC and disciplined allocation, but $3.7T market cap makes multi-bagger, let alone 100x, returns implausible within the satellite mandate.
catalysts: Azure AI capacity monetization
Copilot seat attach rates
Enterprise agreement price increases
risks: Massive AI capex depressing returns on capital
Antitrust/bundling scrutiny
Competitive cloud pricing

scores.thesis: Exemplary capital allocation and fortress balance sheet with ~$1T cap; a defensive core holding, structurally incapable of the asymmetric upside a 100x satellite sleeve requires.
catalysts: Deployment of record cash pile into a large acquisition
Insurance float/underwriting gains
Buybacks below intrinsic value
risks: Post-Buffett succession execution
Cash drag if no large deals
Cyclical exposure via rail/energy/insurance
scores.pass_reason: Mega-cap conglomerate; return profile incompatible with 100x objective.

scores.thesis: Direct-to-unmodified-handset satellite broadband targets a multi-hundred-billion-dollar TAM with a genuine IP/spectrum moat (large phased-array BlueBird design, L-band spectrum, MNO revenue-share deals with AT&T/Verizon/Vodafone/Rakuten). If constellation completion and MNO revenue sharing scale, incremental economics are software-like; however $28B cap already discounts substantial success, cutting the 100x math.
catalysts: Block 2 BlueBird launch cadence and commercial beta service
Definitive MNO revenue-share contracts converting to cash
FCC/spectrum approvals and Ligado/L-band integration
Government/defense contract awards
risks: Heavy dilution and capital intensity to fund full constellation
Launch failures and satellite deployment delays
Starlink Direct-to-Cell competition with superior launch access
Pre-revenue valuation with regulatory dependency

scores.thesis: Only credible Western small-launch operator plus a fast-growing, higher-margin space systems/components business; Neutron could unlock the medium-lift market and vertical integration gives durable cost advantage and an emerging end-to-end space services moat under a founder-CEO with strong execution record. Valuation at ~$50B already embeds Neutron success.
catalysts: Neutron first launch and cadence ramp
Space Systems backlog conversion and Flatellite/constellation ambitions
National security launch contract wins (NSSL Lane 1)
Path to positive free cash flow
risks: Neutron schedule slip and development cost overruns
SpaceX pricing dominance
Persistent losses and dilution
Rich multiple leaves no margin for error

scores.thesis: First commercial entity to soft-land on the Moon; positioned as the prime for NASA CLPS and lunar data relay (Near Space Network) services, an emerging cislunar infrastructure TAM. At ~$3.6B it retains real optionality, but revenue is government-dependent, margins thin, and mission risk binary.
catalysts: IM-2/IM-3 mission success and follow-on CLPS task orders
Lunar Terrain Vehicle and data relay contract awards
Backlog growth and first sustained positive gross margin quarters
risks: Mission failure destroying credibility and share price
Concentration in NASA budget appropriations
Recurring dilution and warrant overhang
Fixed-price contracts with cost overrun exposure

scores.thesis: Roll-up of space infrastructure components (solar arrays, avionics) plus optionality in microgravity pharma manufacturing and the Edge Autonomy drone acquisition. Diversified backlog is attractive, but the acquisitive model, low margins, and leverage undermine the high-ROIC and moat criteria.
catalysts: Edge Autonomy defense drone revenue synergies
European defense/space budget expansion
Microgravity biopharma milestones
Margin improvement on fixed-price backlog
risks: Serial dilution and debt-funded M&A integration risk
Persistent negative EBITDA and cost overruns on fixed-price programs
Customer concentration in government programs
Weak pricing power as a subsystem supplier
scores.pass_reason: Acquisition-driven, low-margin supplier economics with weak moat and dilution history.

scores.thesis: Independent voice AI platform with genuine multi-decade speech IP, edge-capable architecture, and expanding automotive/restaurant deployments in a large conversational-AI TAM. But it competes against hyperscaler foundation models, gross margins have been diluted by acquisitions, and cash burn plus dilution has been heavy.
catalysts: Automotive OEM design wins converting to per-unit royalties
Restaurant/drive-thru voice ordering scale deals
Agentic AI/Amelia enterprise cross-sell
Path to adjusted EBITDA breakeven
risks: Commoditization of voice by OpenAI/Google/Amazon
Customer concentration and lumpy bookings
History of shareholder dilution and accounting restatement
Subscale revenue versus valuation
scores.pass_reason: Moat questionable against hyperscaler LLM commoditization; unit economics unproven.

scores.thesis: Trapped-ion quantum computing leader with high-fidelity qubits, strong patent estate, and a networking/QKD acquisition strategy addressing a potentially enormous long-term compute TAM. However revenue is grant/pilot-driven, cash burn is severe, and $17.6B already prices in commercial quantum advantage that may be a decade away.
catalysts: Roadmap milestones toward logical qubits (Tempo/2M physical qubit targets)
Government and national-lab contract awards
Quantum networking acquisitions creating an integrated stack
Any demonstrated commercial quantum advantage
risks: Competing modalities (superconducting, neutral atom) plus Google/IBM scale R&D
Minimal revenue against enormous valuation
Continuous equity issuance and dilution
Timeline risk: commercial utility may slip beyond investment horizon
scores.pass_reason: Valuation already large relative to negligible revenue; technology and timeline risk too high for high conviction.

scores.thesis: Leading eVTOL developer with vertically integrated manufacturing, deep FAA certification progress, and strategic backing from Toyota, Delta and Uber targeting a large urban air mobility and defense TAM. Certification, if achieved first, creates a formidable regulatory moat, but the business is pre-revenue and capital-hungry.
catalysts: FAA type certification progress and TIA flight testing
Dubai/UAE commercial launch and exclusive operating rights
Toyota manufacturing partnership scaling and additional investment
DoD/Agility Prime contracts and hybrid VTOL programs
risks: Certification delays pushing revenue years out
Massive cash burn and dilution before scale
Unproven consumer demand and unit economics at target price points
Archer and international competition; battery/infrastructure constraints
